content:
Ava: :rotating_light: incidentbot fired: pagerduty.high: routing-latency-threshold (auto) - several noisy pages, check?
incidentbot: PagerDuty incident 358912 triggered: routing-latency-threshold - 7 pages in 2m, auto-escalation enabled.
oncall-bot: @Ava you are the current on-call. To acknowledge, react with :thumbsup: or type `ack`
Ava: acking, will check dashboard now
sam: I can take logs if you want — I’m near a laptop, grabbing p95 and recent traces
lee: seeing a brief bump in router queue length and a spike of 503s from edge-proxy for a few minutes. might be a routing hop flapping.
Ava: good catch. sam — can you run this query on logs-prod?
Ava: ```
# p95 latency last 10m by route
query: sum(increase(request_latency_ms_bucket{le="1000"}[10m])) by (route)
```
sam: running... getting initial: /v1/generate route p95 ~ 1.2s -> baseline is 180ms, small subset of hosts contributing (3 nodes)
jordan: I see the same hosts reporting kernel throttling warnings in metrics: `node_exporter_cpu_iowait` spiked briefly. Might be noisy host-level IO.
lee: also seeing a small increase in 4xx rate from a canary client, but overall success rate remains >99.7%
Ava: customer impact check — any user-facing errors or alerts from support?
sam: slack #support-monitoring shows one ticket about intermittent timeouts from a single enterprise customer, timestamp aligns with spike. Not widespread.
jordan: correlate to dedicated pool? Looks like these hosts were running a batch of model-compile jobs (non-critical) during the window. Could be IO saturation.
Ava: I'm silencing PD for this alert group to stop noisy escalations while we triage. `pd silence` incoming.
Ava: ```
# silencing the routing-latency-threshold policy for 30m
pd silence --service routing-latency-threshold --duration 30m --reason "transient hop flapping, triage in progress"
```
oncall-bot: Incident acknowledged by Ava. PagerDuty silence applied by Ava for 30m.
Ava: sam — can you collect `dmesg` and `iostat` from the three nodes and upload to /tmp/incident-3287659999?
sam: copied logs. small iowait blip, one node shows sustained writes from `/var/tmp/model_compiler` during spike.
lee: temporarily moved compile jobs off the pool, I scaled down compile daemons on those hosts.
jordan: re-routing suggestions: we can mark the 3 hosts as draining in the router, let traffic avoid them for a few minutes: `redwood router drain --hosts x,y,z`
Ava: do it. Prefer graceful drain to avoid long requests failing.
lee: drain initiated, healthchecks passing for remaining hosts.
Ava: monitoring p95 and error rate.
sam: p95 back down to 210ms after drain, 503s dropped to baseline.
jordan: support ticket updated: "We saw brief timeouts during 16:02-16:05 UTC, root cause: transient IO-heavy compile jobs on 3 hosts. Mitigated by draining hosts and moving compiles."
Ava: good. Any follow-ups? I suggest we add a safety throttle to compile jobs during peak traffic windows to avoid hitting router queue.
lee: filing followup doc and a small alert rule change: add compile-job IO guard and a short-term playbook for routing-hop flaps.
Ava: okay to un-silence PD after confirming stable for 5m?
sam: yes, stable for 6m now. no further 503s.
Ava: unsilencing PD.
oncall-bot: PagerDuty silence removed by Ava.
incidentbot: Incident 358912 auto-resolved (no active pages) — summary: transient host IO causing brief routing latency increase, mitigated by draining affected hosts and pausing compile jobs.
Ava: adding this to the rotation notes and handing off to @lee for follow-ups during next shift. Lee — you own the postmortem and remediation items?
lee: will take it, will draft postmortem and PR to add IO throttle on compile job.
Ava: thanks all. closing thread, marking no broad customer impact but one support ticket. :white_check_mark:
sam: :thumbsup: nice quick triage
jordan: good teamwork
lee: will sync with infra to ensure compile scheduler respects traffic windows
Ava: handing off to lee for full follow-up. oncall out. :wave:
